item.title: El Niño, Flooding Put Squeeze on South African Fruit Producers
item.description: South Africa’s high-value fruit exports are under pressure due to adverse weather ranging from winter floods to heat waves linked to the El Niño weather phenomenon, with growers cutting harvest forecasts for grapes and stone fruit.

item.title: Turkey’s Tightening Steps Show Early Signs of Calming Markets
item.description: Turkey’s latest steps to tighten financial conditions are showing early signs of bringing stability to the country’s turbulent markets and slowing the unwind in popular carry trades.

item.title: Brazil Assets Surge as Lula Taps Trabuco as Finance Chief
item.description: Brazilian assets soared as traders sharply repriced interest-rate expectations after President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva tapped banker Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi as finance minister.

item.title: Ofwat Warns Thames Water Rescue Decision Remains Months Away
item.description: The UK’s water regulator has warned it is still months away from making a decision on whether to approve a rescue of Thames Water by its creditors.

item.title: ¿Volverá la derecha al poder en España?
item.description: España vota tras casi tres años de enorme tensión. Las encuestas apuntan a un regreso de la derecha, pero en 2023 también lo hicieron y Pedro Sánchez logró mantenerse en el poder. ¿Qué está en juego esta vez? (Source: Bloomberg)
